The Gentlemen pre-encryption Volume Shadow Copy deletion (vssadmin/wmic) AIActions on Objectives High
Hunts deletion of Volume Shadow Copies via vssadmin, wmic, or WMI PowerShell — the article explicitly recommends behavioural alerts on vssadmin/wmic shadow-copy deletion, which The Gentlemen performs to inhibit recovery immediately before its Go encryptor runs. Rationale: Article explicitly recommends alerting on vssadmin/wmic shadow deletion; the has_all token pairing keeps it tight to the destructive command form used by The Gentlemen ahead of encryption. Cross-checked against: • https://www.huntress.com/blog/the-gentlemen-ransomware-defense-evasion-ttps
ATT&CKT1490
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Veeam/commvault backup pre-snapshot cleanup
  • Sysadmin manually managing shadow storage (vssadmin resize/delete during troubleshooting)
  • Windows Update/DISM servicing that prunes snapshots
  • Disk-imaging or migration tooling
Suppression filter
| where not (InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("veeam.backup.shell.exe","vsnapvss.exe","dismhost.exe") or InitiatingProcessParentFileName =~ "services.exe" and InitiatingProcessFileName =~ "vssvc.exe")
Response runbook
1) Triage: check the parent process and account — legit deletion comes from backup software or an admin, malicious deletion often comes from a scripted/SYSTEM context alongside other Gentlemen artifacts. 2) Contain: if unsanctioned, isolate the host immediately; shadow deletion is a minutes-from-encryption signal — verify backups are offline/immutable. 3) Hunt: on the host look for the gentlemen_system task, EDR-killer driver loads, wevtutil clears, and a single process modifying files en masse (encryption); alert IR.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where (FileName =~ "vssadmin.exe" and ProcessCommandLine has_all ("delete","shadows"))
     or (FileName =~ "wmic.exe" and ProcessCommandLine has_all ("shadowcopy","delete"))
     or (FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe") and ProcessCommandLine has "Win32_Shadowcopy" and ProcessCommandLine has_any ("Delete","Remove"))
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine
| order by Timestamp desc
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where (NewProcessName endswith "vssadmin.exe" and CommandLine has "delete" and CommandLine has "shadows")
     or (NewProcessName endswith "wmic.exe" and CommandLine has "shadowcopy" and CommandLine has "delete")
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, NewProcessName, CommandLine, ParentProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc

id: 7d3e5a12-8b60-4d2c-bb9f-33ee01dd55aa
description: Detects Volume Shadow Copy deletion via vssadmin/wmic/WMI, a Gentlemen pre-encryption recovery-inhibition step
references:

source:windows.security @EventID:4688 ((@Image:(*\vssadmin.exe OR *\VSSADMIN.EXE) @CommandLine:(*delete*shadows* OR *Delete*Shadows*)) OR (@Image:(*\wmic.exe OR *\WMIC.EXE) @CommandLine:(*shadowcopy*delete* OR *ShadowCopy*Delete*)))

The Gentlemen self-propagating Go encryptor: bulk file modification burst AIActions on Objectives Medium
Behavioural hunt for a single process modifying/renaming a large number of files across many directories within a short window — the encryption shape of The Gentlemen's self-propagating Go encryptor (confirmed by Microsoft). Surfaces the initiating binary/hash and flags interpreter parents (rundll32/powershell) per reviewer guidance. Rationale: Microsoft confirms a self-propagating Go encryptor; a count+dcount(folder) burst per initiating process is the article-consistent encryption signature without inventing an unverified file extension, and it projects the binary/hash so analysts can pivot. Cross-checked against: • https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/security/blog/2026/05/28/the-gentlemen-ransomware-dissecting-a-self-propagating-go-encryptor/ • https://darkatlas.io/blog/how-a-go-binary-locks-down-enterprise-networks-in-minutes-the-story-behind-gentlemen-ransomware
ATT&CKT1486
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Bulk media/photo re-encode or batch rename utility
  • Backup or archival software rewriting many files
  • Source-control checkout or large git operation
  • Indexing/AV full-disk operation touching many files
  • Legit disk-encryption (BitLocker/EFS) rollout
Suppression filter
| where not (InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("backup.exe","veeamagent.exe","robocopy.exe","git.exe") or InitiatingProcessSHA256 in (dynamic([])))
Response runbook
1) Triage: identify the initiating binary and hash from the projected columns — check signer/path and whether the parent is an interpreter (rundll32/powershell), a strong ransomware tell. 2) Contain: kill the process and isolate the host immediately; capture a memory image and preserve a sample of the modified files for key-recovery analysis. 3) Hunt: search the fleet for the same binary hash and for hosts reached over SMB (self-propagation), plus preceding shadow-copy deletion and the gentlemen_system task on affected hosts.
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where ActionType in ("FileModified","FileRenamed")
| where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
| summarize FileCount = count(), FolderCount = dcount(FolderPath), StartTime = min(Timestamp), EndTime = max(Timestamp), SampleFiles = make_set(FileName, 6)
          by DeviceName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessSHA256, InitiatingProcessParentFileName, bin(Timestamp, 5m)
| where FileCount > 300 and FolderCount > 20   // >300 files across >20 folders in 5m = ransomware encryption burst shape
| extend SuspiciousParent = InitiatingProcessParentFileName in~ ("rundll32.exe","powershell.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","mshta.exe")
| order by FileCount desc
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventType in ("FileModified","FileRenamed")
| summarize FileCount = count(), FolderCount = dcount(TargetFilePath), StartTime = min(TimeGenerated), EndTime = max(TimeGenerated)
          by DvcHostname, ActingProcessName, bin(TimeGenerated, 5m)
| where FileCount > 300 and FolderCount > 20   // bulk cross-directory modification burst = encryption
| order by FileCount desc
#event_simpleName=FileWritten
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, ContextImageFileName], function=count(as=FileCount))
| FileCount > 300

Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations Command & Control Medium
C2 channel detection via inter-beacon-time stddev / fan-out to single dest.
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1071.004
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic DeviceNetworkEvents
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where RemoteIPType == "Public" and ActionType == "ConnectionSuccess"
| project DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort, Timestamp
| sort by DeviceName asc, RemoteIP asc, RemotePort asc, Timestamp asc
| extend prev_dev = prev(DeviceName, 1), prev_ip = prev(RemoteIP, 1),
         prev_port = prev(RemotePort, 1), prev_ts = prev(Timestamp, 1)
| where DeviceName == prev_dev and RemoteIP == prev_ip and RemotePort == prev_port
| extend delta_sec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, prev_ts)
| summarize conn_count = count(), avg_delta = avg(delta_sec), stdev_delta = stdev(delta_sec)
    by DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort
| where conn_count > 30 and avg_delta between (30.0 .. 600.0) and stdev_delta < 5.0
| order by conn_count desc
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(2h)
| where DvcAction != "Block"
| where ipv4_is_private(DstIpAddr) == false
| summarize ConnCount = count(),
            DistinctMinutes = dcount(bin(TimeGenerated, 1m))
            by DvcHostname, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber
| where ConnCount > 50 and DistinctMinutes > 30   // sustained, not bursty
| order by ConnCount desc

id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d01
status: experimental

references:

Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution Delivery High
User received an external email containing a URL, clicked it, and within 60 seconds the recipient's endpoint spawned a scripting interpreter or network downloader (PowerShell / cmd / mshta / curl / certutil / bitsadmin). This is the high-fidelity shape — a raw "user clicked an emailed URL" query is too noisy to alert on because every Microsoft 365 tenant generates thousands of legitimate clicks per day. The exec-correlation step suppresses the noise to roughly the rate at which a click actually drives onto-host execution, which is the actionable signal. Pair with UC_PHISH_LINK_BYPASS (Safe Links override) and UC_PHISH_LINK_NEWDOMAIN for orthogonal high-fidelity variants.
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1204.001 T1059.001
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Web Endpoint.Processes EmailEvents EmailUrlInfo UrlClickEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s.
// Far higher fidelity than "every clicked URL" — most legitimate clicks
// never spawn a non-browser child process, so the join eliminates the
// 99% of noise that makes a raw click query unactionable.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectClicks = UrlClickEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | where ActionType in ("ClickAllowed","ClickedThrough")
    | join kind=inner (
        EmailEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
        | where DeliveryAction == "Delivered"
        | where EmailDirection == "Inbound"
        | project NetworkMessageId, Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain,
                  RecipientEmailAddress, EmailTimestamp = Timestamp
      ) on NetworkMessageId
    | join kind=leftouter (
        EmailUrlInfo | project NetworkMessageId, Url, UrlDomain
      ) on NetworkMessageId, Url
    | project ClickTime = Timestamp, AccountUpn, IPAddress, Url, UrlDomain,
              Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain, RecipientEmailAddress,
              ActionType;
// Correlate to a non-browser child process spawned within 60 seconds on
// the recipient's device.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                         "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                        "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                        "bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectClicks on $left.AccountName == $right.AccountUpn
| where Timestamp between (ClickTime .. ClickTime + 60s)
| project ClickTime, ProcessTime = Timestamp,
          DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, ClickTime),
          DeviceName, AccountName, RecipientEmailAddress, SenderFromAddress,
          Subject, Url, UrlDomain, ActionType,
          FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by ClickTime desc
// UrlClickEvents has no clean Sentinel-native equivalent. The detection
// pivots to: Office Send→Receive proximity to SecurityEvent 4688 of a
// non-browser child process. Lower fidelity than the Defender version.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectMailUsers = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation =~ "Receive"
    | summarize Subject = any(Subject), Sender = any(Sender)
                by MailboxOwnerUPN, MessageId, EmailTime = bin(TimeGenerated, 1m);
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("\chrome.exe","\msedge.exe",
                                     "\firefox.exe","\outlook.exe","\brave.exe")
| where NewProcessName has_any ("\powershell.exe","\pwsh.exe","\cmd.exe",
                                  "\mshta.exe","\rundll32.exe","\regsvr32.exe",
                                  "\wscript.exe","\cscript.exe","\bitsadmin.exe",
                                  "\certutil.exe","\curl.exe","\wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectMailUsers on $left.Account == $right.MailboxOwnerUPN
| where TimeGenerated between (EmailTime .. EmailTime + 60s)
| project TimeGenerated, EmailTime, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine, Sender, Subject
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Email attachment opened from external sender Delivery High
Attachment delivery + execution by recipient — most common malware initial access.
ATT&CKT1566.001 T1204.002
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Endpoint.Processes EmailAttachmentInfo DeviceProcessEvents
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MalAttachments = EmailAttachmentInfo
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | project NetworkMessageId, RecipientEmailAddress,
              AttachmentFileName = FileName, AttachmentSHA256 = SHA256;

          InitiatingProcessFileName, AttachmentFileName, AttachmentSHA256
// Sentinel doesn't have an attachment-hash table. Best approximation:
// OfficeActivity Send/Receive activity + correlate to host process spawn.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MailWithAttach = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation in~ ("Send","Receive")
    | where isnotempty(MessageId)
    | project EmailTime = TimeGenerated, MailboxOwnerUPN, Sender,

SecurityEvent

title: Office Application Spawning Script Host
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d07
status: experimental
description: |

    cscript, mshta, rundll32, regsvr32 — classic macro / embedded-
    object payload signature.

    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1566/001/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1059
    - attack.t1566.001
    - attack.execution
logsource:
    category: process_creation
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_parent:
        ParentImage|endswith:
            - '\winword.exe'
            - '\excel.exe'
            - '\powerpnt.exe'
            - '\outlook.exe'
            - '\onenote.exe'
            - '\mspub.exe'
            - '\visio.exe'
    selection_child:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\cmd.exe'
            - '\powershell.exe'
            - '\pwsh.exe'
            - '\wscript.exe'
            - '\cscript.exe'
            - '\mshta.exe'
            - '\rundll32.exe'
            - '\regsvr32.exe'
    condition: selection_parent and selection_child
falsepositives:

level: high
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime

    where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe","outlook.exe","onenote.exe","mspub.exe","visio.exe")
      AND Processes.process_name IN ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wmic.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.parent_process_name, Processes.process_name, Processes.process
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
| `security_content_ctime(firstTime)` | `security_content_ctime(lastTime)`

    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe","outlook.exe","onenote.exe","mspub.exe","visio.exe")
      AND Processes.process_name IN ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wmic.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.parent_process_name, Processes.process_name, Processes.process

Ransomware-style mass file rename / extension change Actions on Objectives Medium

DeviceFileEvents

| where files > 200    // empirical: > 200 unique-file renames in 1m by one account on one host

[GHSA / CRITICAL] GHSA-g936-7jqj-mwv8: TSDProxy: Internal proxy auth token forwarded to backend services enables management API escalation

TSDProxy: Internal proxy auth token forwarded to backend services enables management API escalation

Actions on Objectives
Detected
Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration.
Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad).
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → [LLM] Non-TSDProxy backend process connecting to loopback management port 8080
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key.
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking.
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage. → [LLM] TSDProxy internal auth-token replay to localhost management API · [LLM] Unauthorized localhost call to TSDProxy /api/v1 management endpoint
TSDProxy internal auth-token replay to localhost management API AIActions on Objectives High
Hunts a process invoking the tsdproxy management API on 127.0.0.1:8080 while injecting the leaked internal secret header x-tsdproxy-auth-token together with an attacker-controlled x-tsdproxy-id. These header names are unique to tsdproxy (GHSA-g936-7jqj-mwv8) so their presence in a command line is a direct signature of the token-replay privilege-escalation exploit. Rationale: Keys on the two header names (x-tsdproxy-auth-token, x-tsdproxy-id) shown in the article's repro curl, paired with the fixed 127.0.0.1:8080/api/v1 management endpoint — all strings are unique to this vuln so an in-cmdline match is near-zero-FP. Cross-checked GitLab advisory mirror and CVEReports. Cross-checked against: • https://advisories.gitlab.com/golang/github.com/almeidapaulopt/tsdproxy/GHSA-g936-7jqj-mwv8/ • https://cvereports.com/reports/GHSA-G936-7JQJ-MWV8
ATT&CKT1550.001 T1068
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • A maintainer or pentester validating the GHSA-g936-7jqj-mwv8 fix by running the exact repro curl
  • Automated security-scanning tooling replaying the header to confirm the instance is patched
  • Internal red-team exercise reproducing the token-replay chain
  • A developer's shell-history / documentation snippet echoing the curl example that gets captured by process telemetry
Suppression filter
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("tsdproxy") and ProcessCommandLine !has "scanner" and DeviceName !in~ ("pentest-lab")
Response runbook
1) Triage: pull the full command line and the initiating process/user; confirm the source process is a proxied backend (curl/wget/python/node/php) rather than the tsdproxy binary itself, and whether x-tsdproxy-id was set to a non-empty attacker value. 2) Contain: isolate the host/container, rotate the tsdproxy internal token by restarting the service, and set identityHeaders: false pending upgrade to >=1.4.4-0.20260603142855-434819b4421e. 3) Hunt: review management API access logs (/api/v1/proxies, proxy restart/pause, webhook triggers) around the event, and check other backends sharing the tsdproxy host/network namespace for the same header string.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(14d)
| where ProcessCommandLine has "x-tsdproxy-auth-token" or ProcessCommandLine has "x-tsdproxy-id"
| where ProcessCommandLine has_any ("127.0.0.1:8080","localhost:8080","/api/v1/")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(14d)
| where ActingProcessCommandLine has "x-tsdproxy-auth-token" or ActingProcessCommandLine has "x-tsdproxy-id"
| where ActingProcessCommandLine has_any ("127.0.0.1:8080","localhost:8080","/api/v1/")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, ParentProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: TSDProxy Internal Auth Token Replay to Management API
id: a1f4c2e0-8b3d-4c6a-9e21-7f0d5b3a9c11
description: Detects a process injecting the tsdproxy internal secret header (x-tsdproxy-auth-token) with a spoofed x-tsdproxy-id against the 127.0.0.1:8080 management API (GHSA-g936-7jqj-mwv8).
references:
  - https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-g936-7jqj-mwv8
  - https://advisories.gitlab.com/golang/github.com/almeidapaulopt/tsdproxy/GHSA-g936-7jqj-mwv8/
author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2026/07/12
tags:
  - attack.t1550.001
  - attack.t1068
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: linux
detection:
  token:
    CommandLine|contains:
      - 'x-tsdproxy-auth-token'
      - 'x-tsdproxy-id'
  target:
    CommandLine|contains:
      - '127.0.0.1:8080'
      - 'localhost:8080'
      - '/api/v1/'
  condition: token and target
level: high

Unauthorized localhost call to TSDProxy /api/v1 management endpoint AIActions on Objectives Medium
Hunts HTTP requests to the tsdproxy management API path /api/v1/ on port 8080 arriving over loopback — the exact surface an attacker hits after stealing the forwarded token to enumerate proxies or issue admin operations (restart/pause/webhook). Because legitimate management access is Tailscale-fronted, loopback /api/v1 traffic bearing the tsdproxy identity headers is anomalous. Rationale: Uses the concrete management endpoint (/api/v1/proxies) and port 8080 named in the article's repro, scoped to loopback where the token-replay must originate; captures the network-layer view the process-cmdline UC can miss when the attacker replays from a compiled backend rather than curl. Cross-checked against: • https://advisories.gitlab.com/golang/github.com/almeidapaulopt/tsdproxy/GHSA-g936-7jqj-mwv8/
ATT&CKT1550.001 T1068
Data sourcesWeb.Web
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Legitimate tsdproxy self-calls to its own management API over loopback during normal operation
  • Local health-check or monitoring probe hitting /api/v1 on 8080
  • Admin using an SSH tunnel to reach the management UI, appearing as a loopback source
  • Container orchestration readiness/liveness probes against the management port
Suppression filter
| where RequestClientApplication has_any ("curl","python","wget","go-http-client","node") or RequestMethod in ("POST","PUT","DELETE","PATCH")
Response runbook
1) Triage: identify the client user-agent (RequestClientApplication) and method — a curl/python UA or a POST/PUT/DELETE to /api/v1 from loopback is high-suspicion vs the tsdproxy service's own calls. 2) Contain: block external reachability to the management port, rotate the internal token via service restart, and disable identityHeaders. 3) Hunt: correlate with process telemetry (UC token-replay cmdline) on the same host and review whether proxy configs were enumerated or services restarted/paused via the API.
CommonSecurityLog
| where TimeGenerated > ago(14d)
| where DestinationPort == 8080
| where RequestURL has "/api/v1/"
| where SourceIP in ("127.0.0.1","::1") or DestinationIP in ("127.0.0.1","::1")
| project TimeGenerated, SourceIP, DestinationIP, DestinationPort, RequestMethod, RequestURL, RequestClientApplication, DeviceProduct
| order by TimeGenerated desc
source:linux.syslog service:tsdproxy ("/api/v1/proxies" OR "/api/v1/")
WEB
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats summariesonly=t count from datamodel=Web.Web where Web.dest_port=8080 (Web.url="*/api/v1/proxies*" OR Web.url="*/api/v1/*") (Web.src="127.0.0.1" OR Web.src="::1") by Web.src Web.dest Web.dest_port Web.http_method Web.url Web.http_user_agent | `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count from datamodel=Web.Web where Web.dest_port=8080 (Web.url="*/api/v1/proxies*" OR Web.url="*/api/v1/*") (Web.src="127.0.0.1" OR Web.src="::1") by Web.src Web.dest Web.dest_port Web.http_method Web.url Web.http_user_agent | `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
Non-TSDProxy backend process connecting to loopback management port 8080 AIExploitation Low
Surfaces a proxied backend process (curl/wget/python/node/php/shell) opening a connection to 127.0.0.1:8080 — the precondition the advisory calls out for token replay (backend must reach the management port on loopback). Pairs the leaked-token capture with the network reachability that turns it into management-API takeover. Rationale: Grounded in the advisory's stated precondition ('attack requires the backend to reach 127.0.0.1:8080'); scoping to interpreter/CLI processes hitting loopback:8080 catches the reachability step even when the token itself isn't in a logged command line. Higher FP by nature, so hunting-tier. Cross-checked against: • https://advisories.gitlab.com/golang/github.com/almeidapaulopt/tsdproxy/GHSA-g936-7jqj-mwv8/ • https://cvereports.com/reports/GHSA-G936-7JQJ-MWV8
ATT&CKT1528 T1550.001
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic
Expected false positives · estimated rate: high — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • A backend app legitimately configured to call the management API over loopback (e.g., an admin dashboard on the same host)
  • Local monitoring/health-check scripts probing 8080
  • Another unrelated service also listening on 127.0.0.1:8080 (common dev port)
  • CI/CD or debug tooling on the host issuing loopback requests to 8080
  • Interpreter processes performing normal intra-host service calls unrelated to tsdproxy
Suppression filter
| where InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("x-tsdproxy-auth-token","x-tsdproxy-id","/api/v1/")
Response runbook
1) Triage: confirm 8080 on the host is the tsdproxy management listener (not an unrelated dev service) and inspect the initiating process command line for the tsdproxy identity headers. 2) Contain: if the process is an untrusted/compromised backend, isolate the container, rotate the token via service restart, and set identityHeaders: false. 3) Hunt: pivot to process-cmdline telemetry for x-tsdproxy-auth-token on the same aid/host and review management API logs for enumeration or state-changing calls.
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(14d)
| where RemotePort == 8080
| where RemoteIP in ("127.0.0.1","::1")
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("tsdproxy")
| where InitiatingProcessFileName has_any ("curl","wget","python","python3","node","php","ruby","perl","sh","bash")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, RemoteIP, RemotePort
| order by Timestamp desc
ImNetworkSession

| where DstPortNumber == 8080
| where DstIpAddr in ("127.0.0.1","::1")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, SrcIpAddr, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber, NetworkApplicationProtocol, DvcAction

[GHSA / CRITICAL] CVE-2026-50551: SiYuan: Stored XSS to RCE via Unsanitized Attribute View Asset Cell Content

GitHub Security Advisories
2026-07-10 3 use cases 1 technique 4 kill-chain phases detected

SiYuan: Stored XSS to RCE via attribute-view cell rendering in genAVValueHTML()

Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration. → Asset exposure — vulnerability matches article CVE(s)
Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad). → [LLM] XSS payload planted in SiYuan attribute-view storage (data/storage/av/*.json) by non-SiYuan process
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → [LLM] SiYuan Electron desktop spawns shell/LOLBin child (stored-XSS→RCE via nodeIntegration)
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key.
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking.
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage.
SiYuan Electron desktop spawns shell/LOLBin child (stored-XSS→RCE via nodeIntegration) AIExploitation High
Hunts the post-exploitation step of CVE-2026-50551/CVE-2026-54158: SiYuan's Electron renderer runs with nodeIntegration:true, so a stored XSS payload in an attribute-view cell (or the companion CSS-snippet sink) chains to host RCE via require('child_process'). SiYuan.exe is a note-taking app that should never parent a command shell, script host, or download LOLBin — any such child is high-fidelity evidence the XSS fired. Rationale: Anchored on the article's stated RCE primitive (Electron nodeIntegration:true → require('child_process')) with the concrete parent binary SiYuan.exe; a note app parenting cmd/powershell/mshta is near-zero in benign baselines. Corroborated by GitLab GLAD CVE-2026-54158 and the companion CSS-snippet advisory CVE-2026-54067 confirming the same nodeIntegration RCE sink. Cross-checked against: • https://advisories.gitlab.com/golang/github.com/siyuan-note/siyuan/kernel/CVE-2026-54158/ • https://advisories.gitlab.com/golang/github.com/siyuan-note/siyuan/kernel/CVE-2026-54067/ • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-phhp-9rm9-6gr2
ATT&CKT1203 T1059
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • SiYuan plugin/marketplace (Bazaar) package that legitimately shells out for a build/export step
  • User-invoked 'export to PDF/pandoc' style workflow that SiYuan launches via a shell helper
  • SiYuan auto-update process invoking cmd.exe/powershell for install scripting
  • Portable SiYuan launched from a wrapper .bat that re-parents child processes
  • Security/EDR instrumentation re-parenting processes under SiYuan.exe
Suppression filter
| where not (ProcessCommandLine has_any ("siyuan-kernel","--workspace=") or InitiatingProcessCommandLine has "--updated")
Response runbook
1) Triage: pull the full child ProcessCommandLine and SHA256; decode any base64/-enc PowerShell and check for network/download or persistence calls. Note the acting user and whether the session was remote. 2) Contain: isolate the host, kill the child process tree, and quarantine any file it dropped; block outbound to any C2 the child contacted. 3) Hunt: identify the poisoned attribute-view file under data/storage/av/*.json (see companion UC), confirm SiYuan version < 3.7.0, and pivot across all devices syncing the same workspace since the same JSON rides sync and fires on every device that opens the panel.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName =~ "siyuan.exe"
| where FileName in~ ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe","bash.exe","sh.exe","schtasks.exe","reg.exe")
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, FileName, FolderPath, ProcessCommandLine, SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName endswith "\\siyuan.exe"
| where NewProcessName has_any ("\\cmd.exe","\\powershell.exe","\\pwsh.exe","\\wscript.exe","\\cscript.exe","\\mshta.exe","\\rundll32.exe","\\regsvr32.exe","\\bitsadmin.exe","\\certutil.exe","\\curl.exe","\\wget.exe","\\bash.exe","\\sh.exe","\\schtasks.exe","\\reg.exe")
| where SubjectUserName !endswith "$"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, SubjectUserName, ParentProcessName, NewProcessName, CommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: SiYuan Electron Desktop Spawns Shell or LOLBin (Stored-XSS to RCE)

description: Detects SiYuan.exe (Electron, nodeIntegration:true) parenting a command shell, script host or download LOLBin, the RCE step of CVE-2026-50551 / CVE-2026-54158 stored-XSS chains.
references:
  - https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-56mp-4f3v-fgj2
  - https://advisories.gitlab.com/golang/github.com/siyuan-note/siyuan/kernel/CVE-2026-54158/
author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2026/07/14
tags:
  - attack.t1203
  - attack.t1059
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: windows
detection:
  selection:
    ParentImage|endswith: '\siyuan.exe'
    Image|endswith:
      - '\cmd.exe'
      - '\powershell.exe'
      - '\pwsh.exe'
      - '\wscript.exe'
      - '\cscript.exe'
      - '\mshta.exe'
      - '\rundll32.exe'
      - '\regsvr32.exe'
      - '\bitsadmin.exe'
      - '\certutil.exe'
      - '\curl.exe'
      - '\wget.exe'
      - '\bash.exe'
      - '\sh.exe'
      - '\schtasks.exe'
      - '\reg.exe'
  condition: selection
level: high
source:windows.sysmon @EventID:1 @ParentImage:(*\\siyuan.exe OR *\\SiYuan.exe) @Image:(*\\cmd.exe OR *\\powershell.exe OR *\\PowerShell.exe OR *\\pwsh.exe OR *\\wscript.exe OR *\\cscript.exe OR *\\mshta.exe OR *\\rundll32.exe OR *\\regsvr32.exe OR *\\bitsadmin.exe OR *\\certutil.exe OR *\\curl.exe OR *\\wget.exe OR *\\schtasks.exe OR *\\reg.exe)
#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2 ParentBaseFileName=/siyuan\.exe$/i
| ImageFileName=/\\(cmd|powershell|pwsh|wscript|cscript|mshta|rundll32|regsvr32|bitsadmin|certutil|curl|wget|bash|sh|schtasks|reg)\.exe$/i
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, ParentBaseFileName, ImageFileName, CommandLine], function=count())
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where (Processes.parent_process_name="siyuan.exe" AND Processes.process_name IN ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe","bash.exe","sh.exe","schtasks.exe","reg.exe")) by Processes.dest Processes.user Processes.parent_process_name Processes.parent_process Processes.process_name Processes.process Processes.process_id | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | convert ctime(firstTime) ctime(lastTime)
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where (Processes.parent_process_name="siyuan.exe" AND Processes.process_name IN ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe","bash.exe","sh.exe","schtasks.exe","reg.exe")) by Processes.dest Processes.user Processes.parent_process_name Processes.parent_process Processes.process_name Processes.process Processes.process_id | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | convert ctime(firstTime) ctime(lastTime)
XSS payload planted in SiYuan attribute-view storage (data/storage/av/*.json) by non-SiYuan process AIDelivery Medium
Hunts the persistence/plant step of CVE-2026-50551: the malicious cell lives in data/storage/av/<avID>.json and 'rides normal sync', so an attacker with write access to any synced workspace drops it once and it fires on every device that opens the panel. Flags writes to that exact path by a process other than SiYuan's own binaries (i.e. a third-party sync client, backup tool, git, or manual drop) — the delivery vector the advisory describes. Rationale: Uses the exact storage path from the advisory (data/storage/av/<avID>.json) plus the writer-identity discriminator: SiYuan's own kernel writes these constantly, so a third-party writer is the article's stated 'write access to any synced workspace' plant vector. Corroborated by GLAD CVE-2026-54158 confirming 'AV files live under the workspace and ride normal sync'. Cross-checked against: • https://advisories.gitlab.com/golang/github.com/siyuan-note/siyuan/kernel/CVE-2026-54158/ • https://github.com/siyuan-note/siyuan/security/advisories/GHSA-56mp-4f3v-fgj2
ATT&CKT1080 T1565.001
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Legitimate third-party sync of the user's own edits (Syncthing.exe, OneDrive.exe, Dropbox.exe, GoogleDriveFS) writing the av JSON — same channel the attacker abuses
  • git.exe checkout/pull of a workspace kept under version control
  • Backup/restore tooling (Veeam, Duplicati, robocopy) writing av JSON during a restore
  • Manual copy of a workspace between machines via explorer.exe/xcopy
  • SiYuan running from a non-standard binary name in portable deployments
Suppression filter
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("onedrive.exe","dropbox.exe","googledrivefs.exe","syncthing.exe") or FileName !endswith ".json"
Response runbook
1) Triage: open the flagged data/storage/av/*.json and search cell content for HTML breakout / handler strings ('</textarea>','">','<img','onerror=','onload=','javascript:'); identify the writing process and whether it is a sync/backup agent. 2) Contain: if payload strings are present, remove the poisoned row and pause sync for that workspace so it does not re-propagate; snapshot the file for IR. 3) Hunt: enumerate every device syncing the same workspace and check for SiYuan.exe child-process spawns (companion RCE UC) around and after the write time; confirm SiYuan is upgraded to >= 3.7.0 which escapes the text/url/phone/mAsset branches.
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(14d)
| where FolderPath has @"\data\storage\av\"
| where FileName endswith ".json"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("siyuan.exe","siyuan-kernel.exe","kernel.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessFolderPath, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, FolderPath, FileName
| order by Timestamp desc
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(14d)
| where EventType in ("FileCreated","FileModified")
| where TargetFilePath has @"\data\storage\av\"
| where TargetFileName endswith ".json"
| where ActingProcessName !has "siyuan"
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, TargetFilePath, TargetFileName
| order by TimeGenerated desc

File Browser hook-auth pre-auth RCE: filebrowser spawns shell/recon commands (CVE-2026-54088) AIExploitation High
Hunts the File Browser server binary (`filebrowser`) spawning a shell or OS discovery/tooling child process. Under CVE-2026-54088 an unauthenticated attacker injects shell metacharacters into the login username/password, which `os.Expand` substitutes unsanitised into the admin's hook-auth command, causing the `filebrowser` process to execute attacker OS commands. A file server should essentially never spawn `id`/`whoami`/`curl`/`wget`, so any such child is high-fidelity. Rationale: Uses the concrete vulnerable binary name `filebrowser` (parent) plus the article's PoC injection primitive (shell metacharacters `;`/`$(`/backtick and `id`/`whoami` running under the hook command). A file-server process spawning recon/OS tooling is near-zero in benign operation. Cross-checked against filebrowser.org auth docs and auth/hook.go on GitHub. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-m93h-4hw7-5qcm • https://filebrowser.org/authentication.html • https://github.com/filebrowser/filebrowser/blob/master/auth/hook.go
ATT&CKT1190 T1059.004 T1033 T1087.001
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Admin legitimately configured a hook-auth command that shells out to an external auth backend using curl/wget (e.g. validating against an LDAP/OIDC gateway)
  • Custom container entrypoint or healthcheck wrapper also named 'filebrowser' spawning /bin/sh for readiness probes
  • Ops running the filebrowser CLI (`filebrowser config`, `filebrowser users`) interactively from a shell where the parent/child order is inverted
  • Backup/maintenance scripts invoked by a filebrowser-named systemd unit that call uname/hostname
Suppression filter
| where not (FileName in~ ("sh","bash","dash") and ProcessCommandLine matches regex @"^\s*test\s" and not (ProcessCommandLine matches regex @";|\|\||&&|\$\(|\x60"))
Response runbook
1) Triage: pull the full process tree for the alert — confirm InitiatingProcessFileName=='filebrowser' and inspect the child ProcessCommandLine for injected recon (id/whoami/cat /etc/passwd) or separators; correlate to the host's web/reverse-proxy logs for a POST to /api/login in the same second. 2) Contain: isolate the host, stop the filebrowser container/service, and disable hook authentication (set auth.method back to json/proxy) or patch to filebrowser v2 > 2.63.5. 3) Hunt: on the same host look for follow-on egress/reverse shells (UC2), new files under the served directory (webshell/backdoor), new cron entries or SSH authorized_keys, and any outbound connection from the filebrowser process subtree.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName =~ "filebrowser"
| where (FileName in~ ("id","whoami","uname","hostname","curl","wget","nc","ncat","netcat","socat","python","python3","perl","ruby","php"))
    or (FileName in~ ("sh","bash","dash","ash","zsh","ksh")
        and (ProcessCommandLine has_any ("/etc/passwd","/etc/shadow","whoami","uname","/dev/tcp/")
             or ProcessCommandLine matches regex @";|\|\||&&|\$\(|\x60"))
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessFolderPath, FileName, FolderPath, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessCommandLine
| order by Timestamp desc
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where ActingProcessName has "filebrowser" or ParentProcessName has "filebrowser"
| where (TargetProcessName has_any ("/id","/whoami","/uname","/hostname","/curl","/wget","/nc","/ncat","/socat","/python","/perl","/ruby","/php"))
    or (TargetProcessName has_any ("/sh","/bash","/dash","/ash","/zsh","/ksh")
        and (TargetProcessCommandLine has_any ("/etc/passwd","/etc/shadow","whoami","uname","/dev/tcp/")
             or TargetProcessCommandLine matches regex @";|\|\||&&|\$\(|\x60"))
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, ParentProcessName, TargetProcessName, TargetProcessCommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: File Browser Hook-Auth Command Injection - filebrowser Spawns Shell or Recon Binary
id: 6b1f8c2a-9d3e-4f7a-8c1b-2e5a7c9d4f11
description: Detects the File Browser server binary spawning a shell or OS discovery/tooling child, indicative of CVE-2026-54088 pre-auth command injection via the authentication hook.
references:
  - https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-m93h-4hw7-5qcm
  - https://filebrowser.org/authentication.html
author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2026/07/10
tags:
  - attack.t1190
  - attack.t1059.004
  - attack.t1033
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: linux
detection:
  parent:
    ParentImage|endswith: '/filebrowser'
  tool_child:
    Image|endswith:
      - '/id'
      - '/whoami'
      - '/uname'
      - '/hostname'
      - '/curl'
      - '/wget'
      - '/nc'
      - '/ncat'
      - '/socat'
      - '/python'
      - '/python3'
      - '/perl'
  shell_child:
    Image|endswith:
      - '/sh'
      - '/bash'
      - '/dash'
      - '/ash'
  shell_markers:
    CommandLine|contains:
      - '/etc/passwd'
      - '/etc/shadow'
      - 'whoami'
      - '/dev/tcp/'
      - ';'
      - '$('
  condition: parent and (tool_child or (shell_child and shell_markers))
level: high
#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2 ParentBaseFileName=/^filebrowser$/i
| (ImageFileName=/\/(id|whoami|uname|hostname|curl|wget|nc|ncat|socat|python[0-9]?|perl|ruby|php)$/i OR (ImageFileName=/\/(sh|bash|dash|ash|zsh|ksh)$/i AND regex("(/etc/passwd|/etc/shadow|whoami|uname|/dev/tcp/|;|\\$\\()", field=CommandLine)))
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, ImageFileName, CommandLine], function=count())
WEB
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where Processes.parent_process_name="filebrowser" AND (Processes.process_name IN ("id","whoami","uname","hostname","curl","wget","nc","ncat","socat","python","python3","perl","ruby","php") OR (Processes.process_name IN ("sh","bash","dash","ash","zsh","ksh") AND (Processes.process="*/etc/passwd*" OR Processes.process="*/etc/shadow*" OR Processes.process="*whoami*" OR Processes.process="*uname*" OR Processes.process="*/dev/tcp/*" OR Processes.process="*;*" OR Processes.process="*`*" OR Processes.process="*$(*"))) by Processes.dest Processes.user Processes.parent_process_name Processes.process_name Processes.process | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | convert ctime(firstTime) ctime(lastTime)
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where Processes.parent_process_name="filebrowser" AND (Processes.process_name IN ("id","whoami","uname","hostname","curl","wget","nc","ncat","socat","python","python3","perl","ruby","php") OR (Processes.process_name IN ("sh","bash","dash","ash","zsh","ksh") AND (Processes.process="*/etc/passwd*" OR Processes.process="*/etc/shadow*" OR Processes.process="*whoami*" OR Processes.process="*uname*" OR Processes.process="*/dev/tcp/*" OR Processes.process="*;*" OR Processes.process="*`*" OR Processes.process="*$(*"))) by Processes.dest Processes.user Processes.parent_process_name Processes.process_name Processes.process | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | convert ctime(firstTime) ctime(lastTime)
File Browser hook-auth RCE follow-on: reverse shell / egress tooling under filebrowser (CVE-2026-54088) AICommand & Control High
Hunts the File Browser process subtree spawning a reverse shell or ingress/download tool after successful command injection. Distinct from the discovery UC: this targets the C2 stage where the injected command establishes an interactive shell (`bash -i`, `/dev/tcp/`, `nc -e`, `socat`, `mkfifo`) or pulls a second-stage payload (`curl`/`wget` piped to a shell) from the `filebrowser` process. Rationale: Pairs the concrete vulnerable parent binary `filebrowser` with high-specificity reverse-shell/ingress signatures (`/dev/tcp/`, `bash -i`, `nc -e`, `socat`, `curl|wget` piped to shell) from the RCE class described in the advisory. These command-line strings are near-zero-FP and map the exploit to its C2/second-stage phase. Corroborated via filebrowser.org auth docs and the GHSA advisory. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-m93h-4hw7-5qcm • https://filebrowser.org/authentication.html • https://github.com/filebrowser/filebrowser/blob/master/auth/hook.go
ATT&CKT1059.004 T1105 T1571
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Legit hook-auth command that uses curl/wget to POST credentials to an external authentication API
  • filebrowser sidecar/init script that pulls config or TLS certs via curl/wget at startup
  • Admin debugging the container with `docker exec` where the shell's parent resolves to filebrowser
  • Monitoring agent invoking python from within the filebrowser service context for metrics
Suppression filter
| where not (FileName in~ ("curl","wget") and ProcessCommandLine has_any ("https://auth.","/certs/","/token") and ProcessCommandLine !has "/dev/tcp/" and ProcessCommandLine !has "| sh" and ProcessCommandLine !has "|sh")
Response runbook
1) Triage: extract the child ProcessCommandLine and resolve the destination host/port (grep for the IP after /dev/tcp/ or the nc/socat/curl target); check DeviceNetworkEvents on the same host for a matching outbound public connection in the same window. 2) Contain: isolate the host, kill the filebrowser process/container, block the observed C2 IP/domain at the egress firewall, and rotate any credentials/secrets readable by the filebrowser service account. 3) Hunt: search for downloaded second-stage files, persistence (cron, systemd units, authorized_keys), lateral SSH from this host, and repeat the UC1 discovery query to scope earlier recon.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName =~ "filebrowser"
| where FileName in~ ("sh","bash","dash","ash","zsh","ksh","nc","ncat","netcat","socat","curl","wget","python","python3","perl")
| where ProcessCommandLine has_any ("/dev/tcp/","bash -i","sh -i","mkfifo","socat","import socket","import pty","curl ","wget ")
    or ProcessCommandLine matches regex @"(?i)\bnc(\.traditional)?\b.*\s-[ec]\b"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, FileName, FolderPath, ProcessCommandLine
| order by Timestamp desc
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where ActingProcessName has "filebrowser" or ParentProcessName has "filebrowser"
| where TargetProcessName has_any ("/sh","/bash","/dash","/ash","/zsh","/ksh","/nc","/ncat","/socat","/curl","/wget","/python","/perl")
| where TargetProcessCommandLine has_any ("/dev/tcp/","bash -i","sh -i","mkfifo","socat","import socket","import pty","curl ","wget ")
    or TargetProcessCommandLine matches regex @"(?i)\bnc(\.traditional)?\b.*\s-[ec]\b"
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, TargetProcessName, TargetProcessCommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc

id: c4a7e2b9-1f6d-4b3a-9e08-7d2c5a1f8b34
description: Detects the File Browser server binary spawning a reverse shell or ingress/download tool, indicative of CVE-2026-54088 post-exploitation C2 activity.
references:

author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2026/07/10

logsource:

detection:

    Image|endswith:
      - '/sh'

      - '/dash'
      - '/nc'
      - '/ncat'
      - '/socat'
      - '/curl'
      - '/wget'
      - '/python'

      - 'mkfifo'

      - 'import socket'

| ImageFileName=/\/(sh|bash|dash|ash|zsh|ksh|nc|ncat|socat|curl|wget|python[0-9]?|perl)$/i

| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where Processes.parent_process_name="filebrowser" AND Processes.process_name IN ("sh","bash","dash","ash","zsh","ksh","nc","ncat","socat","curl","wget","python","python3","perl") AND (Processes.process="*/dev/tcp/*" OR Processes.process="*bash -i*" OR Processes.process="*sh -i*" OR Processes.process="* -e /bin/*" OR Processes.process="*mkfifo*" OR Processes.process="*socat *" OR Processes.process="*import socket*" OR Processes.process="*import pty*" OR Processes.process="*curl *" OR Processes.process="*wget *") by Processes.dest Processes.user Processes.parent_process_name Processes.process_name Processes.process | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | convert ctime(firstTime) ctime(lastTime)
Asset exposure — vulnerability matches article CVE(s) Reconnaissance High
Match vulnerability scanner output to the CVE(s) named in the article.
ATT&CKT1190
Data sourcesVulnerabilities DeviceInfo DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
// TVM tables are daily snapshots — pin a 1-day window so the engine
// partitions on Timestamp instead of scanning the full retention.
DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where CveId in~ ("CVE-2026-54088")
| join kind=inner (DeviceInfo | where Timestamp > ago(1d)) on DeviceId
| project DeviceName, OSPlatform, CveId, VulnerabilitySeverityLevel, RecommendedSecurityUpdate
| order by VulnerabilitySeverityLevel asc, DeviceName asc

// Sentinel has no native TVM table. If MDE→Sentinel streaming is enabled,
// `DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities` is available. Otherwise this UC has
// no Sentinel translation — track via Update / Heartbeat OS-version
// gaps as a coarse approximation.
DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)
| where CveId in~ ("CVE-2026-54088")
| join kind=inner (DeviceInfo | where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)) on DeviceId
| project DeviceName, OSPlatform, CveId,
          VulnerabilitySeverityLevel, RecommendedSecurityUpdate
| order by VulnerabilitySeverityLevel asc, DeviceName asc
APPLICATION
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Vulnerabilities
    where Vulnerabilities.signature IN ("CVE-2026-54088")
    by Vulnerabilities.dest, Vulnerabilities.signature, Vulnerabilities.severity, Vulnerabilities.cve
| `drop_dm_object_name(Vulnerabilities)`
| sort - severity
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Vulnerabilities

    by Vulnerabilities.dest, Vulnerabilities.signature, Vulnerabilities.severity, Vulnerabilities.cve
| `drop_dm_object_name(Vulnerabilities)`

Remote service execution — PsExec / SMB lateral movement Actions on Objectives High
psexec / paexec / smbexec / wmic /node — service install over SMB from remote host.
ATT&CKT1021.002 T1569.002
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceProcessEvents
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where FileName in~ ("psexec.exe","psexesvc.exe","paexec.exe","smbexec.py")
   or (FileName =~ "wmic.exe" and ProcessCommandLine has "/node:")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by Timestamp desc

SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4688            // process-create (audit-policy required)
| where Account !endswith "$"
| where NewProcessName endswith "\psexec.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\psexesvc.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\paexec.exe"
   or (NewProcessName endswith "\wmic.exe" and CommandLine has "/node:")
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, NewProcessName, CommandLine,
          ParentProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc
